newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RANGERS STUMBLE BUT FINALLY EDGE THE SHARKS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RANGERS STUMBLE BUT FINALLY EDGE THE SHARKS.

text.p: Niklas Sundstrom scored 84 seconds into overtime as the New York Rangers blew a two-goal third-period lead before snapping their eight-game winless streak with a 5-4 victory over the San Jose Sharks on Monday.

Luc Robitaille's shot from the slot went wide but he tracked down his own rebound in the right corner and carried around the net. He threw the puck in front and it caromed off the skate of defenceman Vlastimil Kroupa directlty to Sundstrom, who beat goaltender Ed Belfour low to the glove side for his 20th goal of the season.
"It always feels great to win, I don't know what happened, I think it was a rebound, I just turned and shot it and it went in," Sundstrom said.
It was the 500th assist of Robitaille's career.
Ulf Samuelsson scored twice and Bruce Driver and Mark Messier also tallied for the Rangers.
At Colorado, Peter Forsberg scored twice and Patrick Roy made 32 saves as the Colorado Avalanche continued their dominance over the struggling Vancouver Canucks with a 5-1 victory.

Keith Jones had a goal and two assists and Scott Young added a goal and an assist for the Avalanche, who have won eight of their last 10 games. Colorado, which became the first team to reach 40 wins, leads the league with 88 points.
Trevor Linden tallied the lone goal for Vancouver, which has lost five of its last six games.
In Toronto, linemates Wendel Clark and Steve Sullivan had a goal and an assist apiece and Felix Potvin turned aside 27 shots as the Toronto Maple Leafs defeated the Boston Bruins, 4-2.
Sullivan, acquired last week from New Jersey, has scored in each of his three games with the Maple Leafs.
Darby Hendrickson and Jamie Macoun added goals for Toronto.
Ray Bourque scored twice for the Bruins.
